solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Outline redraft of the numberless outlines

indicators.note: a redraft reworks text, so the letters that follow are put into a new order
with no number: N, the usual abbreviation for number, is taken away

explanation.surface: An editor asks for a fresh draft of some outlines, with all the numbering stripped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'numberless' removes N from THE OUTLINES; 'redraft of' rearranges the ten letters left. 'Outline' at the start is the definition, echoing 'outlines' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark shape seen only against a lighter background is an outline of something with no inner detail.

clue.text: Record losing men securing border proposal?

indicators.note: securing means holding something fast inside, so one piece is placed within another
losing means the following letters are dropped from the word before

parts.note: to score is to record, as in keeping the score of a game
OR, other ranks, is the military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers
a hem is the finished border of cloth

explanation.surface: A record of a meeting, minus the soldiers, with a frontier attached: a diplomatic proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' are OR, other ranks, which 'losing' removes; 'securing' wraps the remainder round a border. The question mark admits a scheme is only loosely a proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan put forward for consideration is a proposal; the question mark admits the slight stretch.

clue.text: Negligent about navy guarding unknown internal channel

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer word wraps what follows

parts.note: lax means careless or negligent

indicators.note: guarding means surrounding something to protect it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
Y, like X, is a mathematician's unknown

explanation.surface: A careless sailor is slack around naval security on some unidentified waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: The voice box is a passage inside the throat, so an internal channel for air.

clue.text: Mitre would suggest this elevated position?

parts.note: rearrange (put in a new order) the letters of the word merit and you get mitre

explanation.surface: A bishop's tall hat hints at its wearer's lofty rank.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as instructions (an order, i.e. anagram, of MERIT), produces MITRE. A mitre is a tall bishop's hat, which also suits 'elevated'.
explanation.definitionFit: Membership of the Order of Merit is one of the highest honours, a lofty place in a ranking.

clue.text: Some at supper will consume them

definitions.text: Some at supper will consume them

indicators.note: the words before swallow up the answer, so its letters lie inside them

explanation.surface: Diners at an evening meal will eat certain things.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is inside 'somE AT Supper'; the whole clue also defines it, since what diners consume is food.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal for food, the very thing people at a meal swallow.

clue.text: Inform American about a rave (or energetic dance)

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pieces go around the next ones

parts.note: to tell is to inform
to rant is to rave

explanation.surface: Someone tells an American off for ranting, or perhaps it is just a lively dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the inform-American pair round 'a rave', splitting it after its first letter; the parenthesis just tacks on the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fast whirling folk dance from southern Italy, named after Taranto.

clue.text: Like the writer is, mostly in a land far away

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: like means as, the writer is I, and is for I becomes am

explanation.surface: A writer says they are, for the most part, in a distant country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like the writer is' gives AS I AM; 'mostly' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent of the Orient is far away from Britain, where the clue was written.

clue.text: Broadcast match including hour and minute when things kick off?

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the short letters go into the longer words

parts.note: to sow is to broadcast seed by scattering it

indicators.note: and here repeats the including for the second word, so the minute also sits inside the match word

parts.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: A televised football match gets its time slot: the hour and minute of kick-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts H into SOW and M into TIE. The question mark flags 'kick off' as figurative: it is when a show starts.
explanation.definitionFit: The moment a performance begins is the time things start, to kick off in the general sense.

clue.text: Vexatious refusal adopted by some in Government at first

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in by, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'
no is a refusal

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A ministers' refusal proves irritating to some in government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopted by' sets the refusal inside 'some'; 'at first' takes just the opening letter of Government.
explanation.definitionFit: Vexatious and irritating are synonyms: both describe something causing annoyance.

clue.text: Journal after this point covers time of family development

indicators.note: after means the journal comes after the other piece

parts.note: here means at this point

indicators.note: covers means wraps around, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a diary is a journal

explanation.surface: A diary records, from now on, how a family's story develops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' wraps the journal round the time letter, and 'after' puts that behind 'this point'. The definition is adjectival: concerning how a family line passes things on.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereditary traits come down through the family line, so they concern how a family develops.

clue.text: Fail to stop thug

definitions.meaning: to carry on, to continue without halting
a hired heavy or ruffian, a hoodlum's muscle

explanation.surface: A thug who can't stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means continue; as one it is slang for a hired heavy.

clue.text: Start working in the AA, entering Institute

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the anagram goes inside the other word

parts.note: to found is to institute or establish

indicators.note: working means set in motion, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone starts a job at the motoring organisation by joining its institute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' shuffles IN THE AA (the AA being Britain's Automobile Association, a breakdown service) into TAINHEA; 'entering' sends it into the word for institute.
explanation.definitionFit: A source or origin is where something starts, like the spring of a river.

clue.text: Incantation: piece taking skill in reflection

indicators.note: taking means the first piece takes on the next one after it

parts.note: a man is a piece in chess or draughts

indicators.note: in reflection means seen in a mirror, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: art is skill

explanation.surface: A spell: a chess piece captures a skilful move while the player reflects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in reflection' flips the skill word to TRA; 'taking' just joins it on behind the chessman.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or chant repeated in meditation or magic is a kind of incantation.

clue.text: Ineligible? Thrown out during University year

indicators.note: during means inside the time span, so the anagram sits between the outer letters
out means put out of order, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student deemed ineligible is expelled during their university year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles 'Thrown' into NWORTH; 'during' sets that between the university and year letters. 'Ineligible?' and 'Thrown out' both suggest expulsion, a nice blend.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not deserving of a thing is unfit for it; the question mark marks the loose equivalence with ineligible.

clue.text: In the event, it's the last thing you expect to come across

definitions.text: In the event, it's the last thing you expect to come across

parts.words: In the event, it's the last thing you expect to come across
parts.note: in a race (an event) the final line you cross is the one at the end; the idiom 'the last thing you expect' misleads

explanation.surface: Something that turned up was the very last thing anyone expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the event' looks like 'as it turned out' but means in a sporting event; 'come across' means find, but here cross literally.
explanation.definitionFit: In a race the marked line at the end is the last thing runners cross, ending the event.

clue.text: Doctor returning during famine, once energised, for treatment of migrant workers?

indicators.note: during means inside, so the reversed doctor sits within the shuffled letters
energised means stirred into action, so all these letters are shaken into a new order
returning means coming back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: MD is a doctor of medicine

explanation.surface: A doctor comes back to a famine-struck land, once full of energy, to treat migrant labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' makes DM, put 'during' FAMINE; 'energised' rearranges that with ONCE. 'Treatment' is a literary treatment: Steinbeck's novella about itinerant ranch hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Steinbeck's novella follows two itinerant ranch hands in Depression-era California, a literary handling of migrant labour.

clue.text: Flight science? I crashed in river — the reverse of scientific

indicators.note: crashed in means burst into, so the letter goes inside the river

parts.note: the Avon is an English river

indicators.note: the reverse of means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: sci is a short form of scientific, as in sci-fi

explanation.surface: A pilot explains how a flight came down in a river, a most unscientific event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed in' sends I into the river; 'the reverse of' turns the short form of scientific into ICS. The surface's 'crashed' suggests an aircraft, fitting the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The electronics on an aircraft are its flight technology; the question mark admits that this is engineering, loosely a science.

clue.text: Endless clamour has sharp effect on political meeting

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a hue, as in hue and cry, is a clamour
stings means has a sharp, painful effect

explanation.surface: Constant shouting makes a pointed impact on a political gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts HUE to HU.
explanation.definitionFit: Hustings are the meetings where election candidates address voters, a political gathering.

clue.text: One's used to show invalid value after reprogramming

indicators.note: a reprogrammed value is reworked, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A program flags an invalid value once it has been rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's used to show' means one who is used to performing in shows, not a tool for showing something.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety performer is accustomed to appearing in stage shows, so one used to show business.

clue.text: Hoax leads to unfortunate arrest — I'm before Judges

parts.note: to josh is to tease or hoax

indicators.note: leads means the first letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A prank leads to a regrettable arrest, and the prankster now stands before the judges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judges' is the book of the Bible, not a court: the answer's book comes just before it.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament the book named after Moses' successor directly precedes the Book of Judges.

clue.text: Angry leader retaining only half of team

indicators.note: retaining means holding within, so the half goes inside

parts.note: a head is a leader

indicators.note: only half of means the first two of the four letters are kept

explanation.surface: A furious captain keeps only half of the squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half of' keeps TE from team, and 'retaining' has the leader hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated argument is an angry one: tempers have risen.

clue.text: Old upper-class mean to protect Queen for definite

parts.note: U is the label for upper-class usage

indicators.note: to protect means surrounding to guard, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: tight means mean with money
R is from Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A stingy old aristocrat is certainly set on guarding the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to protect' puts R inside TIGHT, after O and U.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright and definite both mean complete and beyond question, as in an outright winner.

clue.text: Invite admission revealing switch in components in funding

indicators.note: the two parts of the phrase change places, so the second word goes in front

parts.note: come in is what you say to invite someone to enter

explanation.surface: An invitation to enter shows a change in parts of the financing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch in components' swaps the two words of COME IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Money coming in, such as revenue, is a source of funding.

clue.text: High-level apartment falling short (one with limited technology)

indicators.note: falling short means the final letter is lost

parts.note: a loft is an apartment high up in a building
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A top-floor flat proves inadequate for someone with only basic gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling short' cuts LOFT to LOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-fidelity recording uses basic, cheap equipment, so it is made with limited technology.

clue.text: Legal establishments in both ends of the country?

parts.note: north and south, N and S, are the two extremes of a country

explanation.surface: Law firms found at the far north and far south of the land.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inns of Court are the four London societies that train and admit barristers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inns of Court are the professional bodies of English barristers, so legal establishments.

clue.text: Give greeting to thespian in play

indicators.note: in play means put into motion, so these letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor in a stage play is greeted by the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in play' rearranges TO THESPIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising one's headwear slightly is a traditional way to say hello.

clue.text: Insolent behaviour implying no change in character?

parts.note: read the letter S as the letter S: a character (letter) left unchanged

explanation.surface: Cheekiness that suggests someone's personality hasn't changed at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' means a letter, not a personality: S as S describes a letter left unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sass is informal for cheek or impudence, rude behaviour.

clue.text: Not keeping up location of clock face?

definitions.meaning: lagging, in arrears or late with payments or work
a clock's dial sits at the back of its pointers

explanation.surface: Falling behind, and the spot where a clock's face lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as one word it means late; split, it says the dial sits at the rear of a pointer.
